implementation_notes: Combine supplies the channel: PassthroughSubject broadcasts elements to all downstream subscribers, replacing the observer registry with a publisher value you send() into; each subscriber is a Subscription (sink/assign) whose AnyCancellable token is the unsubscribe. Choose it when subscribers need composition operators and typed payloads; the subject drops values when no subscriber or no demand exists.
pitfalls: A PassthroughSubject drops values when there are no subscribers or current demand is zero - it buffers nothing.
Subscriptions live only as long as their AnyCancellable token: not storing it releases the subscriber immediately and it receives nothing.
Subjects are reference types shared across threads; sending from multiple queues without serialization breaks Combine's demand accounting.

variants.name: NotificationCenter broadcast
variants.implementation_notes: Foundation's NotificationCenter is a notification dispatch mechanism that enables the broadcast of information to registered observers: observers register for a notification name, optionally scoped to a sender object, and post() broadcasts to every registered observer. It predates Combine and remains the right tool when the publisher is framework or system code that cannot expose a Combine publisher, or when observers live across module boundaries.
pitfalls: Observer registration must be removed explicitly (removeObserver or the returned token); a selector-based observer that is deallocated while still registered can crash on the next post.
Notification names are global strings: a typo means a subscriber never fires, and a name collision means unrelated modules suddenly receive each other's events.
post() delivers synchronously on the posting thread; observers that block hold up the publisher, and observers that post again can recurse.
